claims.text: An integrated AIMD and ML-enhanced thermodynamic-integration framework can accurately and efficiently predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across compositionally diverse HEAs.
The target initial state is a chemically disordered, near-equiatomic HEA solid at ambient pressure.
AIMD thermodynamic integration on a representative subset of HEAs can provide training data for an ML surrogate that generalizes across the HEA family.
Capturing short-range atomic arrangements and local distortions in the disordered solid and liquid embeds relevant local coordination environments and volume fluctuations in the predictions.
AIMD thermodynamic integration across melting can compute the free energies needed to estimate melting temperature.
AIMD thermodynamic integration can quantitatively estimate enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, and volume change at melting.
An ML surrogate can rapidly predict phase-change properties across broader HEA composition space by learning correlations from the AIMD simulation data.
The surrogate addresses the inefficiency of direct AIMD while maintaining high accuracy.
Traditional analytical approximations often assume defect-free, idealized crystals.
The framework is expected to predict HEA melting temperatures with errors below ±5%.
Fusion enthalpy, entropy of fusion, and volume change at melting are expected to be predicted with similarly improved quantitative accuracy relative to experimental or calorimetric data.
Liquid heat capacity and thermal-expansion coefficients are expected to be predicted within an approximately ±5% error margin.
Rule-of-mixtures and empirical or idealized-crystal baselines typically have errors exceeding ±10–15%.
Existing analytical and empirical baselines have limited applicability across HEA compositional diversity.
The proposed approach is expected to apply to single-phase, chemically disordered HEAs for which the underlying interatomic description is well defined.
The approach may be less reliable for HEAs with strong segregation, ordering, extreme atomic-size or chemistry mismatch, or inadequate representation in the training set.
Transferability of the ML surrogate to out-of-sample HEA compositions remains unvalidated.
AIMD cost may restrict the density of training data for chemically complex systems.
The approach is to be falsified if measured melting properties consistently deviate from predictions by more than ±5% across the tested HEA composition range.
The approach is also to be falsified if predicted composition-dependent trends are not experimentally observed.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention describe generalization across the HEA family or entire HEA family, whereas the boundary restricts expected applicability to single-phase, chemically disordered systems and excludes several important HEA regimes.
